text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-4821 fired for service=redwood-runtime, region=us-east-az2, symptom=high-75p-token-latency > threshold. Auto-page to oncall SRE.

pagerduty: PD-4821 — fired (unacknowledged) — @maria oncall-sre (rotation: liam -> maria)

maria: seeing it. I’m on it. Starting triage — grabbing metrics and recent deploys.

ken: noted increased 95th latency in the console graphs ~ 10:44 UTC. Could be autoscaler thrash or GPU eviction. Pulling node logs now.

maria: thanks. sasha, can you check the routing layer (edge -> az2) and any recent routing policy changes?

sasha: no config pushes in last 2 hours. Routing rate to az2 spiked ~10:42 UTC then dropped. Looks like sudden traffic drop then backlog replays causing bursts. Link: https://console.redwood/metrics/az2/traffic (internal)

liam: PD shows repeated 502 from inference backends in az2 before the latency spike. Could be pod evictions. Getting k8s events.

maria: paste recent k8s events and top OOM/KILL:

maria: ```
kubectl -n runtime get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -n 20
10:41:12 Pod runtime-gpu-7 OOMKilled
10:41:19 Pod runtime-gpu-3 Evicted
10:42:05 Pod runtime-gpu-5 CrashLoopBackOff
```

ken: confirmed OOMs on several GPU nodes. Memory pressure on az2 nodes. Possibly a caching regression + increased prefix cache size. We rolled a small runtime tweak yesterday.

maria: good catch. Rollback candidate? Any canary running?

sasha: canary rollout stopped at 10:30 due to a config gate but the runtime tweak was promoted at 09:50 in the dedicated config service.

ken: I’ll revert the runtime knob that increased kv-prefix prefetch from 64MB -> 256MB. That should free memory. Rolling hotfix now.

maria: do it, but be careful—we need graceful restarts. Start with az2-only.

ken: issuing rollback:```
/ops/rollback --service runtime --region us-east-az2 --target-tag v1.4.7
```

deploy-bot: Deploy command received and queued: rollback runtime v1.4.7 -> executing in az2.

pagerduty: PD-4821 — acknowledged by maria.

liam: any customer-facing impact? Anna, can you surface affected customer signals?

anna: checking logs and support tickets. Spike in 502 rate for a handful of customers started 10:40 UTC. No billing incidents yet. Opening a short incident note to CS.

anna: Draft message for affected customers (internal):
> We observed elevated latencies and transient errors for requests routed to us-east-az2 between 10:40–10:55 UTC. We have rolled back a recent runtime change and are monitoring. No data exposure.

maria: rollback in progress — trackers show pods terminating and new ones recycling. Monitoring memory and 95p latency.

ken: rollback status: 6/8 nodes updated, 2 still draining. Memory pressure dropping.

maria: good. Can we enable temporary cross-region routing to shift new traffic away from az2 for the next 15m? We should avoid customer retries piling up.

sasha: enabling routing policy: set prefer-region us-east-az1 for new sessions, fallback to az2 if needed. Applying now.```
/routing/apply --policy prefer-region --from us-east-az1 --to us-east-az2 --duration 15m
```

sasha: policy applied. Expected propagation ~30s.

anna: I’ll push update to support and set a banner for customers using affected endpoints.

maria: latency graph breathing — 95p down from 1.2s -> 250ms. Backends 200 OK returning.

ken: pods stabilized. OOMs stopped after rollback. Looks like the prefetch mem regression was root cause.

liam: Excellent. I’ll keep PD on watch for 30m and ensure no auto-escalation.

pagerduty: PD-4821 — status: acknowledged -> resolved (auto) at 10:55 UTC after monitor cleared.

maria: marking incident as mitigated. Creating a short post-incident note with timeline, root cause (kv-prefix prefetch change), and recommended follow-ups: 1) tighter memory regression test in canary; 2) circuit-breaker for prefix prefetch; 3) temporary routing guard rails.

ken: I’ll open the PR for a revert-proof test and quantify mem delta.

sasha: I’ll add a routing policy that can be toggled by SRE for fast regional drain.

anna: CS message posted to affected customers and triage channel. No escalations to legal or execs.

maria: handing off to liam for the next 4h watch. Please post any anomalies here.

liam: taking 4h watch. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — great coordinated response. Closing thread after follow-ups filed.
